items.headline: Stocks mixed Nov. 18: Dow drops 1.1% on Fed minutes, S&P 500 slips for a fifth day, Nasdaq edges up
items.note: The Dow fell 561.25 points to 50,198.17, the S&P 500 fell 0.23% to 7,323.63 (its longest losing streak since June) and the Nasdaq rose about 0.4% to 24,429.88. Fed minutes pointing to more rate hikes and weak healthcare stocks weighed on the Dow. This is the latest close I confirmed; Thursday's close wasn't available yet.

items.headline: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 a share, above the range, with trading as ANT set for Thursday
items.note: Per reports, it sold at least $68B of stock, plus a $26B private placement at the same price, valuing it near $1.49T fully diluted (per the Financial Times). Orders were close to seven times the shares offered. Nasdaq says ANT lists Nov. 19; I couldn't find its opening price or first-day close, and the price itself was reported via sources rather than announced.

items.headline: Nvidia fell 2.9% even after $115.8B in revenue and a ~$130B forecast
items.note: Revenue was up 103% from a year earlier, but the stock gave up an early rally as investors weighed the CEO transition after Jensen Huang's departure and doubts about how long heavy AI infrastructure spending can last. A good report no longer guarantees a rising stock.

items.headline: Fed minutes: nearly all officials expect a December rate hike
items.note: The minutes from the Oct. 27–28 meeting say nearly all officials expect a quarter-point hike in December, and two floated a half-point move; the rate was held at 3.9% in October, with two governors dissenting in favor of a hike. A 'vast majority' worry inflation could persist. Higher rates tend to pressure tech and growth stocks.

items.headline: OpenAI introduces GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
items.note: OpenAI describes gains in professional work, coding and computer use at lower compute cost, per a digest of Nov. 18 news. I only saw summaries, so check OpenAI's own page for specifics. New models like this shift what's expected of ML interns on agent and coding tools.

items.headline: Administration reportedly weighs requiring disclosure of Chinese AI model use
items.note: Fox News reports the idea is under consideration, not a finalized rule. If adopted, it could affect which open-weight models companies are allowed to build on.

items.headline: Tech layoffs top 142,000 this year, but data science skills hold up better
items.note: Layoffs.fyi counts 142,000+ tech layoffs at 350 companies in 2026 as of Nov. 11. Postings analyses show statistics and ML in 92% of data science listings, though entry-level roles in AI-exposed fields have been squeezed. Figures come from secondary summaries, so treat them as approximate.

items.headline: NYC startups keep raising: Hatz AI lands $24M in AlleyWatch's weekly roundup
items.note: AlleyWatch's review of Nov. 8–14 lists the $24M AI deal; the prior week saw 6 deals and $216M+ invested. A steady stream of AI startups in the city means more local internship targets.

learn.term: Opening auction (why a new stock's first trade differs from its IPO price)
learn.explain: An IPO price is what the company's banks sell shares for the night before. Once trading starts, the Nasdaq runs an opening auction: it collects buy and sell orders and finds the single price where the most shares can trade. That opening price can be well above or below the IPO price. Anthropic priced at $83 for its ANT debut, but the first trade could land elsewhere depending on demand. Investors who got shares at $83 gain or lose from there.
learn.try: Look up the first-day 'pop' of a recent big IPO and compare its IPO price to its opening price.
